regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the quality check is less flattering. IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirm investment-led momentum, but core sector slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and passenger vehicle sales have decelerated two consecutive months to 7.9% YoY — the consumption engine is idling while the capex engine runs. The divergence matters: investment-led growth without consumption broadening is a one-cylinder story, and the cylinder is running on credit, not income.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is the number RBI must explain; decompose it and the architecture is uncomfortable. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print, rising for two months — is doing the heavy lifting, while core CPI at 3.9% YoY sits at the 28th percentile. The inversion: benign core gives RBI cover to hold, but fuel at this level feeds into transport costs, which feed into food logistics, which feed back into CPI with a one-to-two quarter lag. The pause is defensible today; it becomes harder to defend by Q1 FY28.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence, widening for two consecutive months — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 73rd percentile historically. Services credit at 24.3% YoY and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY are the accelerators; housing credit at 11.1% YoY is falling for the second month, suggesting the consumer is borrowing for mobility and services, not assets. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while credit was accelerating, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending — the incentive structure for a repeat circular is intact.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting. With CPI at 5.54% YoY, the real repo rate is barely positive at roughly zero — insufficient to anchor inflation expectations if fuel and food pressures persist into Q4. RBI's own inflation forecast has moved to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%, a 50 bps revision that the market has not fully priced. A rate cut in this environment would be a gift to inflation; a hike would stress the CD ratio further. The RBI is parked in a corridor with no comfortable exit.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — rising for two consecutive months — and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity, up from 75.6%, confirm the investment upcycle is not a statistical artefact. The threshold that historically triggers private capex acceleration is 80% utilisation; at 77.4%, India is close but not there. Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY suggests corporates are borrowing to invest, not just to refinance — a qualitatively different signal. The risk: if the CD ratio forces banks to slow credit growth, the capex cycle loses its funding bridge before utilisation crosses the trigger.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹203,521 cr / month is a 73rd-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the level. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural and semi-urban demand recovering — the informal economy is participating. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY, falling for two months, and commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY, also falling two months, suggest urban discretionary and freight demand are softening. E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY sits at the 15th percentile. The GST number is partly formalization reclassifying existing spend; the vehicle and e-commerce data are harder to flatter.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence that has widened for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY prior), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), agriculture at 17.2% YoY (78th percentile), vehicle at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile). Housing credit lagging at 11.1% YoY, falling for 2 months. Credit card growth collapsed to 3.6% YoY (28th percentile lo).","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike as CD ratio stays elevated. Services and vehicle lending are the growth engines; housing is cooling. Expect RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months if divergence persists. Reduce exposure to credit-dependent consumer finance (personal loans, credit cards).","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios above 85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19). The acceleration in credit growth to 19.4% is at 75th percentile, signalling late-cycle lending behaviour.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest, up from 16.1% YoY prior) — 52nd percentile, but rising 2 months in a row. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 74th percentile. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (50th percentile, down from 5% but still positive). Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (74th percentile), agriculture at 17.2% YoY (78th percentile), services at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile). Office absorption surging at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), up from 2.81 mn sq ft / quarter prior — though data is volatile. Home loan disbursements at 19,900 ₹ cr / quarter (latest), up from 15,920 ₹ cr / quarter prior.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks — capex cycle is broadening beyond IT infrastructure into real estate, agriculture, and services. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% leaves room for 3-5% more growth before bottleneck pricing kicks in. Favour banks with high exposure to project finance and working capital lending (Axis, ICICI, HDFC). Avoid consumer discretionary until capex-driven employment gains flow through to wage growth (2-3 quarters lag).","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile historically preceded 18-24 months of steady capex. IIP capital goods at 52nd percentile is moderate but the 2-month uptrend and broad credit acceleration across sectors signal early-to-mid cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, Affluent Rotation Underway","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,490 ₹ cr / month (latest), rising 3 consecutive months (29,845→31,961→32,297→32,490). At 93rd percentile historically. SIP accounts at 10.0646 mn (latest), but SIP AUM at 17.86 ₹ lakh cr — implying average ticket size of ₹17.75 lakh per account, up from ₹16.64 lakh cr / 10.45 mn = ₹15.9 lakh per account 3 months ago. SIP YoY growth at 10.7% (30th percentile lo), but absolute inflows accelerating. Equity MF net inflows at 38,307 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 29,329 ₹ cr net / month prior), at 80th percentile. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (95th percentile hi). FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (17th percentile lo) — persistent outflows.","implication":"SIP growth is decelerating in account count (10.7% YoY) but accelerating in AUM — affluent retail is entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour; expect SIP growth to plateau within 6 months. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (Nifty 50 constituents) where affluent SIPs concentrate. Underweight small-cap and mid-cap where retail SIP concentration is highest — they will face redemption pressure when growth slows. FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month are a headwind; monitor for reversal if Fed cuts rates.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile have historically preceded 2-3 quarter plateaus followed by 10-15% drawdowns. Average ticket size rising is a classic late-cycle signal — mass retail enters early, affluent enters late.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Pause","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior) — 95th percentile hi, a 2-month rising streak. Brent crude at 104.9 $/bbl (flat), but recent trend shows 110.1→110.7→111.2→112.3→113.4→111.9 $/bbl over last 6 months (up 4 of last 5). WTI at 96.69 $/bbl (flat), recent trend 100.7→101.9→102.5→103→104.1→102.4 $/bbl (up 4 of last 5). FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5), at 61st percentile, rising 2 of last 3 months. Food inflation at 7.74% YoY (up from 5.97% YoY), at 57th percentile, rising 2 months in a row. Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83% YoY), at 52nd percentile. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile lo).","implication":"RBI's rate pause is at risk if fuel inflation stays above 20% YoY for another month. Expect RBI to signal hawkish bias in next policy (likely 25-50 bps hike by Q2 FY27). Overweight defensive sectors (FMCG, pharma, utilities) with pricing power. Underweight auto, airlines, and logistics where fuel is a major cost. Hedge INR weakness — oil imports will pressure CAD if Brent stays above 110 $/bbl. Long crude oil futures as a hedge against stagflation.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded RBI rate hikes within 4-6 weeks. The last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% YoY was 2022, which triggered 190 bps of hikes over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Cycle Accelerates, Yen Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (latest, up from 1% p.a. prior), at 100th percentile hi — rising 2 consecutive months (0.75%→1%→1.25%). Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (up from 3.75% p.a.), at 69th percentile mid, rising 2 in a row. US 10Y Treasury yield at 4.94% (down from 4.98%), at 89th percentile hi. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25% p.a.), at 63rd percentile mid, rising 2 in a row. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (up from 56), at 91st percentile hi, rising 2 in a row. Global PMI composite at 54.3 index (up from 53.5), at 84th percentile hi, rising 2 in a row. DXY at 101.831 index (flat), at 55th percentile mid. US VIX at 21.15 index (flat), at 16th percentile lo.","implication":"BOJ's aggressive tightening (100th percentile) is unwinding the yen carry trade — expect INR to weaken further as carry traders unwind long rupee positions. Reduce long INR exposure; hedge with USD forwards. Expect US Treasury yields to stay elevated (4.8-5.1% range) as Fed stays hawkish despite inflation moderating. Overweight USD-denominated assets and underweight EM equities. Monitor for sudden yen appreciation (>5% move) which would trigger forced deleveraging in carry trades and spike VIX.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile tightening is unprecedented in this cycle; the last time BOJ raised rates this aggressively was 2006-07, which preceded the 2008 crisis. Yen carry unwinds have historically spiked VIX by 300-500 bps within weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens to 95.24, FII Outflows Persist","data_text":"INR/USD at 95.24 ₹ (latest, up from 94.89 ₹ prior) — at 89th percentile hi, weakening trend 96.15→97.09→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24 ₹ over 6 months (up 2 of last 5, volatile). FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (latest), at 17th percentile lo, persistent outflows. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (95th percentile hi), offsetting FII. India VIX at 15.5 index (up from 15.3), at 11th percentile lo — complacency despite INR weakness. US 10Y Treasury at 4.94% yield (down from 4.98%), at 89th percentile hi. Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (up from 3.75% p.a.), at 69th percentile mid.","implication":"INR weakness is structural — FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month are not being offset by RBI intervention (no reserve depletion visible). Expect INR to test 96-97 ₹/USD within 2-3 months if FII outflows persist. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto) who benefit from INR weakness. Underweight importers (oil, metals, electronics). Hedge INR exposure for corporates with USD liabilities. Monitor RBI's reserve adequacy — if reserves fall below $600 bn, expect RBI to tighten liquidity and raise rates.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness has historically preceded 2-3 quarter periods of 3-5% further depreciation. FII outflows at 17th percentile lo are persistent; the last time FII outflows lasted > 3 months was 2022, which saw INR weaken 8% over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks GCC Consolidation, Not IT Recovery","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, up from 2.81 mn sq ft / quarter prior) — appears bullish at first glance. But cross-domain check: Nifty IT index flat (recent: 22,600→22,753→22,750→22,699→22,937→23,053 index, up 3 of last 5 but no momentum). IT credit growth at 18.2% YoY (74th percentile), but this is INDUSTRY credit (includes non-IT services). Services credit growth at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile) — this is the real driver. Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (down from 14.5%), at 36th percentile lo. Rent in Bengaluru at 103.6 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 102.5), at 59th percentile mid. Rent in Mumbai at 156 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 144.4), at 59th percentile mid. But: Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (up from 85.17), at 35th percentile lo — weak corporate travel. E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY (15th percentile lo), down from 18% YoY prior — retail footfall not accelerating.","implication":"Office absorption is driven by Global Capability Centers (GCCs) consolidating space, NOT traditional IT services expansion. GCCs are capital-light, high-margin operations for MNCs — they don't drive employment or wage growth like IT services did. This is a false positive for consumption. Underweight commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) — GCC demand is concentrated in 3-4 prime locations and will plateau once consolidation ends. Avoid betting on office-driven consumption recovery; airline traffic and e-commerce growth are the true consumption proxies, and both are weak. Watch for GCC hiring announcements — if they slow, office absorption will reverse sharply.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"This is a non-obvious cross-domain insight: office absorption is rising while IT stocks are flat and airline traffic is at 35th percentile lo. Historical precedent: 2015-16 saw similar office absorption spikes driven by GCC consolidation, followed by 2-year plateau and 15-20% price corrections in commercial RE.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Investment Engine Running — Consumption Cylinder Misfiring

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, with IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — the investment upcycle is real.
  • But passenger vehicle sales decelerated to 7.9% YoY for a second consecutive month, and commercial vehicle sales fell to 12.6% YoY — freight and urban discretionary softening simultaneously.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural demand is alive; e-commerce GMV at 12.4% YoY (15th percentile) says urban digital consumption is not.
  • Core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile) gives RBI statistical cover; fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is the trapdoor beneath it.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is investment-led and credit-funded — not income-led and consumption-broadened. When the credit cycle tightens, the growth number has less structural support than the headline implies.

Bottom line: Watch capacity utilisation: a print above 80% of capacity would validate private capex acceleration; a stall here confirms the cycle is bank-dependent, not demand-driven.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Re-acceleration Meets BOJ Tightening — EM Carry at Risk

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile, rising two in a row) and US GDP SAAR accelerating to 3.4% SAAR from 2.2% — the US is not slowing.
  • But BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — a 10-year high, rising three consecutive months from 0.75% — is the underappreciated pressure valve for yen-funded carry trades.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.94% yield (89th percentile) with Fed Funds at 3.88% p.a. — the curve is pricing neither cuts nor distress, just duration risk.
  • Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY (rising two in a row) with ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. — Europe is tightening into a 1.2% YoY GDP print.

The tension: DM equity markets are pricing re-acceleration; DM central banks are still tightening. BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the specific mechanism by which this resolves — yen carry unwinds hit EM liquidity before the Fed moves.

Bottom line: BOJ's next meeting is the event to watch: a move to 1.5% p.a. would trigger yen carry unwind with direct INR and FII flow consequences within 30–60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — FII Exit Offsets the Celebration

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile, rising three consecutive months) with DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr net / month (95th percentile) — domestic absorption is structural.
  • But FII equity net at -₹49,935 cr net / month (17th percentile) — persistent outflows nearly offsetting DII inflows, leaving net domestic equity flow barely positive.
  • MF AUM fell to ₹82.64 lakh cr from ₹87.08 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion despite record SIP inflows signals equity market weakness beneath the flow headline.
  • NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) — retail is buying existing funds, not new themes; risk appetite is narrowing even as ticket sizes rise.

The tension: Record SIP inflows coexist with falling MF AUM and near-record FII outflows — the domestic bid is real but it is absorbing foreign selling, not driving price discovery higher.

Bottom line: If FII outflows sustain above -₹40,000 cr net / month for a third consecutive month, DII absorption capacity will be tested and Nifty support at 22,700 becomes the line to watch.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Bid Holds Premium Segment — REIT Prices Signal Office Doubt

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 2 pp), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, price +6% YoY, 28 months unsold inventory — supply is running ahead of absorption.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter is GCC-driven (41% of occupier mix); IT services at 22% of mix with Nifty IT flat — the absorption surge is not an IT recovery.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 10–28% from prior — the listed market is not pricing the absorption data.

The tension: Physical office absorption is rising on GCC demand; REIT unit prices are falling. Either the listed market is wrong about occupancy sustainability, or GCC leases are shorter-duration than the headline absorption implies.

Bottom line: Avoid REIT exposure until Embassy or Mindspace reports occupancy above 90% with lease tenure above five years — the absorption data alone does not justify re-rating.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — BOJ Lights the Match

The facts:

  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising three consecutive months) — yen carry unwind risk is the highest-probability external shock; INR at 95.24 (89th percentile) has no buffer.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising two months) with Brent trending $110–113/bbl over six months — every $10/bbl adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill and widens CAD ~40 bps.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if deposit growth stalls, a macro-prudential risk-weight circular is the regulator's next move.
  • But India VIX at 15.5 (11th percentile) — the market is pricing none of these risks; complacency is itself a risk multiplier.

The tension: Three independent stress vectors — external carry unwind, domestic inflation overshoot, and credit-deposit divergence — are each individually manageable; their simultaneous arrival is not priced anywhere in Indian volatility markets.

Bottom line: Watch BOJ's next policy decision: a move to 1.5% p.a. is the single data point that converts latent risk into active positioning — FII outflows and INR weakness would accelerate within days.

"}
